newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Koreans may have killed civilians, Seoul says.
newsitem.headline: N.Koreans may have killed civilians, Seoul says.

text.p: South Korea's defence ministry said it suspected that the three South Korean civilians found dead on an east coast mountain on Wednesday were killed by North Korean infiltrators.

Two men were found shot dead while a 67-year-old women was suffocated after she was battered by a heavy object. The men, aged 54 and 45, were reported missing on Tuesday after they failed to return home from picking mushrooms.
"We suspect the remnants of the North Korean infiltrators were responsible," a ministry statement said. A search of the area was launched after residents reported hearing two gunshots.
South Korean troops found empty M-16 rifle cartridges with no serial markings next to the bodies, which were carefully concealed by grass.

Last month a North Korean submarine landed 26 agents on an east coast beach. Of these, 22 were killed by Southern troops or found dead, one was captured alive and a hunt is under way for the other three.
